summary: Pool of randomised character definitions for the 'random character' button of character creation (gui::DCCharacterCreation RandomCharacterIndex/Count). Created by bg3.exe+0x2027B00 with 16 slots.

structs.name: RandomCharactersCharacterDefinition
structs.equals: Script Extender character_creation::CharacterDefinition (Components/CharacterCreation.h, 0x288 bytes: int field_0, STDString Name, BaseCharacterDefinition, Appearance, abilities, LevelUpData) - game type eoc::character_creation::BaseDefinition

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: first 4 bytes, moved as a uint32 by the element move in bg3.exe+0x6DA880; SE field_0

fields.name: Name
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x6DA880 moves a 24-byte string at +8 (resets the source to the empty SSO state: size 0, capacity 0xF); SE Name

fields.name: Rest
fields.evidence: rest of SE CharacterDefinition (BaseCharacterDefinition at +0x20, Appearance at +0xC8 moved by eoc::character_creation::Appearance::Appearance, abilities, LevelUpData) - kept as bytes here

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x201D030 and the initialiser bg3.exe+0x2027B00 write -1 to the whole 8 bytes +0..+8 (macOS InitializeRandomCharactersComponent the same). Probably the current random index (GUI exposes RandomCharacterIndex); width not established - may be one 64-bit value.

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: second half of the 8-byte -1 store; see field_0.

fields.name: Definitions
fields.evidence: Creator zeroes the array at +8; destructor bg3.exe+0x6ACB30 resizes it to 0 with bg3.exe+0x6DA880 (element stride 0x288, element dtor FUN_1406CF3C0) and frees it; bg3.exe+0x2027B00 resizes it to 16. macOS: ls::DynamicArray<eoc::character_creation::BaseDefinition>::Resize(.., 0x10).

open_questions: Meaning and width of the 8 bytes at +0 (always -1 when written).
Element kept as bytes after Name (SE CharacterDefinition).
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Not settled: as for RandomAppearances - the Windows users only build views (bg3.exe+0x208DA70 / 0x208E300 / 0x1F8A050), and the command processor that reads the 8 bytes at +0 has no matched Windows function; the element remains SE CharacterDefinition kept mostly as bytes.
